q: Does the observed decay rate of Li's VDAMR divergence-flag fraction under mesh refinement change when the divergence operator is switched from central finite differences (this replication) to the paper's median-dual vertex-centred FV divergence (Navier2D)?
basis: Our manufactured verification uses a bona-fide analytical streamfunction so central-difference divergence is O(round-off) and shrinks with dx only through floating-point noise (2e-16 -> 2e-13 across 5 halvings, flag_frac 0.147 -> 0.0005). A vertex-centred FV median-dual discretisation on the same field would give a true O(dx^2) truncation-error divergence that shrinks quadratically. The paper's stated indicator behaviour and any claimed convergence rate are only interpretable in the paper's own discretisation.
next_steps: Implement the median-dual FV divergence operator in Python (or download Engwirda's Navier2D MATLAB code and re-run the manufactured field through it). Re-run the 6-grid sweep. Fit log-log slopes of max|div|, mean|div|, and flag_frac vs dx; compare to expected O(dx^2). Then repeat under a NON-solenoidal test velocity field (e.g. u = (sin(pi x)cos(pi y), -cos(pi x)sin(pi y)) + eps * curl-free noise) to expose the AMR flag's sensitivity to genuine incompressibility violation.

q: How does the paper extract the vortex-centre location from the numerical solution: raw psi-minimum, bulk-flow-subtracted psi-minimum, or |velocity|-minimum? The three give substantially different y-coordinates in our manufactured field (0.164 vs 0.35 vs still elsewhere).
basis: Our recovered argmin(psi) converged to yc=0.164 despite the geometric Gaussian centre being at yc=0.35. Reason: Poiseuille background psi increases with y from the wall, so adding a negative bump shifts argmin toward the wall. Armaly/Erturk conventions vary in the literature; we could not resolve which the paper uses because we cannot read the paper. This single ambiguity would flip a claimed ~5% match into a ~100% mismatch.
next_steps: (a) Cross-check Li's sibling papers (Li & Wood 2016 JCAM, Li 2024 MDPI Mathematics 12(18):2831 which IS open access) for their exact vortex-centre extraction procedure. (b) Instrument our synthetic verifier with all three extraction methods in parallel and quantify the sensitivity: report (xc, yc) for each on the same dx-sweep, so subsequent replicators can compare apples-to-apples regardless of the paper's convention. (c) If Rick approves the DOI paywall bypass through library ILL, get the actual paper and settle it.

q: Why did our stream-function/vorticity BFS solver fail to develop primary recirculation at 3 of 4 (Re, dx) points while the sibling replication's Chorin-projection MAC-grid solver did on the same coarse meshes at the same Re?
basis: Our solver produced wall-shear that stayed positive everywhere downstream of the step at Re in {100, 200, 50 at dx in {0.1, 0.075, 0.25}}, indicating flow immediately re-attached. Only Re=50 dx=0.15 gave a proper vortex (x_r/S=1.78). The sibling's Chorin solver saw x_r/S in the 4.4-4.7 range at Re=100 across dx=0.25 to 0.10. Both solvers use first-order upwind convection. Suspect: (i) our Thom boundary-vorticity at the reentrant corner (x=xs, y=hs) is under-resolved / singular; (ii) our Neumann psi-outlet (copy from Nx-2) creates a rigid mass-flow constraint that damps upstream separation.
next_steps: (a) Implement a proper convective outlet BC (Orlanski-type: du/dt + c*du/dx = 0 with c=umax) instead of psi-copy. (b) Handle the reentrant corner with a corner-averaged Thom rule (Woods' formula) or explicit corner-vorticity computation from the analytical solution of a viscous corner-flow problem. (c) Cross-validate by porting the sibling's MAC-grid Chorin solver to the SAME test case and diff'ing the recirculation profile point-by-point. (d) As a sanity check, try FEniCS/dolfinx with Taylor-Hood elements on the SAME geometry; it should give a clean textbook BFS.

q: What is the minimum resolution h/dx (cells per step-height) required for VDAMR to correctly identify the primary vortex location in the actual BFS-NS problem, and does that minimum grow with Re?
basis: The sibling replication used dx=0.25 (4 cells per unit step-height) and got a coherent answer; we needed dx=0.15 (~7 cells) for the one case that worked. The paper claims 'refine as many times as required'; but presumably there is a minimum initial resolution below which the flow does not even qualitatively resemble BFS. This is quantitatively important for practitioners (compute budget) and no BFS-AMR paper I am aware of has systematically documented it.
next_steps: Once a robust BFS-NS solver is in place (see Q3), sweep h/dx in {2, 4, 8, 16, 32} at Re in {50, 100, 200, 400, 700}. Report the coarsest h/dx that recovers x_r/S within 10% of a converged fine-grid reference at each Re. Fit h/dx_min(Re) empirically; expect scaling with sqrt(Re) if boundary-layer resolution dominates. This directly quantifies AMR's practical starting-mesh requirement.

q: Does the paper reconcile the three-way Reynolds-number convention mismatch (Li's u_avg-based Re vs Armaly-1983 u_max-based Re_D = 3*Re_Li vs Erturk-2008 u_max-based Re_e = 1.5*Re_Li) when it compares vortex-centre locations across sources?
basis: For an ER=2 BFS parabolic-inlet flow, u_max = 1.5 * u_avg upstream, so Armaly Re_D = 2h * u_max/nu = 3 * u_avg * h / nu = 3 * Re_Li and Erturk Re_e = h * u_max/nu = 1.5 * Re_Li. This is a factor-of-2 disagreement between Armaly and Erturk on the SAME physical operating point, and papers routinely mix conventions. The abstract we have does not mention this. If the paper implicitly compares Li Re=100 to Armaly Re=100 (rather than Armaly Re_D=300), any claimed 'agreement' would hide a factor-of-3 physical mismatch.
next_steps: (a) Once the paper is obtainable (library ILL), grep for 'Reynolds', 'Re_D', 'u_max', 'u_avg', 'hydraulic diameter'. (b) Cross-check with Li 2024 MDPI Mathematics 12(18):2831 (OA) which likely uses the same convention. (c) Publish a small comment/note tabulating all four common BFS Reynolds conventions side-by-side; this is a recurring source of confusion in the AMR-CFD literature. (d) Any downstream metanalysis of BFS-AMR should insist on paper authors reporting BOTH u_avg-Re and u_max-Re.
